newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end pit trading mostly firmer.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end pit trading mostly firmer.

text.p: Key IMM currencies ended mostly firmer after a day spent consolidating recent losses.
Floor traders said volume had died down again, with rollover into December futures and expiration of September contracts now completed.
September IMM currency futures went off the boards quietly at 0915 CDT/1415 GMT on Monday, an expiration that floor brokers said proceeded with even less fanfare than usual.
Currencies on Monday glossed over another session of big gains in the U.S. stock market, which had rallied on Friday and compounded pressure on major currencies.
The Dow 30 Industrials by late afternoon had added more than 62 points and cleared the 5900 level for the first time ever.
"The stock market, we're a little leery about seeing that continue higher, but it doesn't seem to be helping the dollar that much today," said one currency floor broker.
They said players instead still were adjusting to the currency downturn that began in early September.
"It just seems like a little (long) dollar profit-taking," the broker added. "Last week it seemed like the funds were long currencies, got flat and reversed."
Some traders expected currencies to keep edging upward nearterm as shorts continue to take profits.
"I'd probably say there might be a little more (long dollar) profittaking coming...a little more currency upside," said another floor broker.
"Basically, there's indecision," added another broker. "People don't want to buy the dollar at these levels and they also don't want to take positions."
They said they doubted, however, that Tuesday's August U.S. capacity use and industrial output figures would rouse much interest.
Capacity use was forecast edging up to a 83.3-percent rate from July's 83.2-percent reading. Output was expected to rise 0.4 percent after a 0.1-percent increase in July.
Some waited for Wednesday's July U.S. trade balance report, expected to show a widening in the gap to $8.8 billion from June's $8.1-billion shortfall.
Futures, which began barely mixed, advanced to the day's peaks as European trading wound down but lacked upside followthrough and backed down again.
EMU concerns lingered, with comments by German and British officials on Monday underscoring the uncertainty.

Bank of England governor Eddie George said economic conditions for EMU remain "somewhat unpromising." Separately, he told a newspaper the dispute between Britain, Germany and France over access to future EU interbank payment system threatened to undermine cooperation among central banks.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said rumors that rules for monetary union would be eased were "totally baseless."

Dec yen rose $0.000021 to $0.009191, marks up $0.0009 to $0.6657, Swiss fr rose $0.0015 to $0.8130, pound rose $0.0026 to $1.5570, Can dollar off $0.0004 at $0.7326, Aussie dollar fell $0.0020 to $0.7864, Mex peso fell $0.000200 to $0.126100. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
